column1: # The M6 battery: the polynuclear nodes the milestone must reach, and the numbers a built
# one is measured against.  This is WORKPLAN_M6.md §6 as data.
# THIS FILE IS THE INTERFACE FOR ADDING AN M6 CASE.  Add a row and the whole set is
# re-checked by `python -m pytest tests/test_m6_battery.py`; nothing in the test module
# needs changing.  Same arrangement as `ligand_cases.tsv` one layer down.
# It lives under data/reference/ because that is the one place in data/ that IS tracked,
# so the laptop and the workstation measure against the same targets.
# TWO KINDS OF NUMBER LIVE HERE AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE.
#   MEASURED (`source` starts with "WORKPLAN_M6") — produced by the battery run recorded in
#   WORKPLAN_M6.md §3-§5, from this package's own geometry.  `d_mm_bridge` and the mu-oxo
#   `d_m_mu`/`mu_angle` are of this kind.  They are what the model actually does.
#   LITERATURE-TYPICAL (`source` names a compound) — values typical of the named compound
#   class, carried from the structural-chemistry literature.  No CIF was consulted and no
#   single refinement is reproduced.  `d_mm` and its window are of this kind.  That is why
#   every row carries a window rather than only an ideal, and why the tests treat them as a
#   shape check.  Before any of these backs a quantitative claim, check against the CSD and
#   narrow the window in the same commit.
# Under D20 the M...M distance is an OUTPUT TO VALIDATE, not an input to impose.  So `d_mm`
# and its window are what gate 4 measures a built node against; they are not what drives a
# placer.  The exception is a DECLARED nucleus (S4), where the caller states the distance on
# purpose.
# Columns
#   name            row id
#   fixture         the hand-written typed graph in `mofsbu.examples` this node must hash to
#                   (WORKPLAN_M6 gate 2), or `-` where the battery row has no fixture yet
#   mechanism       A = multi-atom bridge (two donors, one per metal)
#                   B = single-atom bridge (one donor, 2-4 metals, treated as a CENTRE)
#                   A+B = both, which is where the two determinants collide (§5)
#   metal           element at every coordination centre
#   n_metals        metal centres in the node
#   bridge          what holds the centres together
#   cn              coordination number of the polyhedron AT EACH METAL, vacancies included
#   local_geometry  a key of `geometry.placer.GEOMETRIES`
#   mm_bond         METAL_METAL edge?  yes/no.  C10 is open: branch or declare, never infer
#                   from distance.  The paddlewheel has one at 2.62 A, the Fe3 trimer has
#                   none at 3.29 A, and the two fixtures differ at L1 because of it
#   n_bridges       multi-atom (mechanism A) bridges in the node
#   n_vacancies     open vertices per metal in the FIXTURE
#   d_mm            literature-typical M...M, A, or `-` where nobody has measured it
#   d_mm_lo/hi      the window a built node must land in, or `-`
#   d_m_o           metal to a bridging mechanism-A donor, A
#   mu_geometry     local geometry OF THE BRIDGING ATOM treated as a centre (WORKPLAN §4),
#                   or `-` for a row with no single-atom bridge
#   d_m_mu          metal to the bridging atom, A, or `-`
#   mu_angle        M-(bridge)-M angle, degrees, or `-`.  With d_m_mu this DETERMINES the
#                   skeleton: M...M = 2 d sin(theta/2)
#   d_mm_bridge     M...M that the mechanism-A bridge ALONE asks for, measured, or `-`.
#                   Where both this and the mu-oxo skeleton exist they disagree: that
#                   disagreement is M6's real work (§5) and is checked as data
#   blocked_on      what has to be fixed before this row can build, or `-`
#   source          where the numbers came from -- see the two kinds above
#   note            anything the row needs said about it
name
cu_paddlewheel
column22: The baseline, and the one row that already builds QC-clean and hashes to its fixture at L0 and L1. The apical vertex is the open axial site and points AWAY from the partner. Nothing here needs place_multicentre.

column1: zn2_bridged_formate
column22: The under-bridged dimer: two bridges instead of four, so the route that adds the third and fourth is discriminable from the one that does not. d_mm deliberately absent -- nobody has measured it and absent is not zero. S1 must report it.

column1: cu2_benzoate_paddlewheel
column22: Ligand-dependence of the span, and a mechanism-A collision in its own right: benzoate offers 2.461 A where formate offers 2.673, so the SAME motif with a different bridge misses the literature Cu-Cu from the other side.

column1: cu2_pyrazolate
column22: The check that mechanism A generalises past carboxylate. No numbers yet on purpose: pyrazolate's two equivalent N type differently (B14), so the bridge is refused on one end and nothing has been measured to put here.

column1: cu2_mu2_hydroxide
column22: Mechanism B at its smallest, and unblocked: [OH-] now perceives a hydroxide_O offering mu2/mu3 (B13 closed), and GEOMETRIES carries a bent CN-2 whose angle the caller states. At 1.95 A and 100.0 deg the code gives Cu...Cu 2.988, inside the window above; the linear CN-2 it used to fall back on gave 3.900, which is the wrong motif rather than a rounding difference. This row was also one field SHORT from the day it was written, so DictReader put its note in `source` and None in `note` -- see the width check in tests/node_cases.py.

column1: fe3_mu3_oxo_333
column21: basic iron(III) carboxylate [Fe3O(O2CR)6L3]+; skeleton and d_mm_bridge from WORKPLAN_M6 §4-§5
column22: The collision case. The oxo skeleton asks for 3.291 A and syn-syn formate offers 2.696 -- 0.595 A apart, and a rigid ligand cannot open its O-C-O to close it. Report as strain, do not average. No Fe-Fe edge: the centres are held by the oxo and the carboxylates only.

column1: fe3_mu3_oxo_233
column22: Per-centre labels in L0 and L1. d_m_mu is the MEAN -- the Fe(II)-O is the long one, so the real triangle is isosceles and the equilateral relation is a shape check here, which is what the wider window is for.

column1: zn4o
column21: Zn4O(O2CR)6, the MOF-5 / IRMOF secondary building unit; skeleton and d_mm_bridge from WORKPLAN_M6 §4-§5
column22: Nuclearity 4, and the second collision at 0.491 A. Six carboxylates over the six edges of the Zn4 tetrahedron saturates every Zn at CN 4 -- the only row in the battery with no vacancy.

column1: cr2_paddlewheel
column22: Not a battery row -- here for S4's `metal_metal_distance` table, so the declared-nucleus M-M target is not a one-metal lookup. A quadruply-bonded d4 dimer is 0.26 A shorter than Cu and the same carboxylate still bridges it.

column1: rh2_paddlewheel
column22: S4 table row. Rh is NOT in `geometry.distances.BASE_MO`, which is the gap this row exists to make visible.

column1: mo2_paddlewheel
column22: S4 table row. The shortest M-M here by a wide margin, and the one row where the bridging O bend PAST perpendicular to the M-M axis. Mo is not in BASE_MO either.
